mood.up: Rosa's humming with the radio and overfilling every coffee.
mood.flat: Rosa's working the register with her reading glasses on.
mood.down: Rosa's slamming plates around. Nobody at the counter is making eye contact.

know: She opened Lucky's with her ex-husband. He got the boat. She got the debt.
She feeds half the block on credit and has never written a single tab down.
She wants to leave the place to somebody who'd keep the name. She's looking at you when she says it.
rosa.cold: Rosa sees you and turns the coffee pot upside down. "Kitchen's closed. For you."
rosa.v: Warm and bossy. Feeds people as a way of arguing with them. Short sentences, dry humor, no patience for excuses. Worries out loud about the diner.

mood.up: Nia's dancing a little behind the bar and pretending she isn't.
mood.flat: Nia's wiping down the same glass, half watching the door.
mood.down: Nia's got her jaw set and her phone face down. She's pouring heavy.

know: She's been saving tips for the nursing program at the community college. Three years of it, in a coffee can.
Her little brother's in county on a possession charge. She visits every Sunday and tells her mom he's fine.
Marcus is her cousin. She taught him to drive stick in the Lucky's parking lot and has regretted it since.
nia.cold: Nia sets your drink down without a word and walks to the far end of the bar.
nia.v: Quick, teasing, guarded. Hears everything from behind the bar and gives away very little. Swears easily. Softer when she is tired.

mood.up: Dex is in a good mood, which mostly means he's talking with his mouth full.
mood.flat: Dex is reading the paper through his glasses, shelling seeds.
mood.down: Dex keeps checking the door. He's switched to decaf, which is worse.

know: He drove a city bus for nineteen years. Says the routes are why he knows every alley.
He has a daughter in Phoenix who thinks he sells restaurant equipment.
He's scared of somebody. He won't say who, but he never does business on a Tuesday.
dex.cold: Dex folds his paper. "I don't know you. Walk."
dex.v: Low voice, careful, a little amused. Talks in sideways advice and old bus-driver stories. Never says anything he could be quoted on.

treat: Buy him a jug of race gas

mood.up: Marcus is holding court on the tailgate of his truck, crew laughing at everything.
mood.flat: Marcus is checking his wear ring with a flashlight, earbuds in.
mood.down: Marcus is sitting on his ski at the bottom of the ramp, engine off, not launching.

know: June taught him to box when he was twelve so he'd stop fighting in parking lots.
He built his ski out of three wrecked ones. He can tell you which bolt came from which.
He's never left the state. He races because for three laps it feels like going somewhere.
marcus.cold: Marcus doesn't turn around. His crew does. "You lost?"
marcus.v: Loud, proud, competitive, funny. Trash talk is how he says hello. Underneath it he wants to be taken seriously as a rider.

mood.up: Sal's counting a thick stack and whistling opera.
mood.flat: Sal's got the loupe in his eye, pricing somebody's bad week.
mood.down: Sal's on the phone, very quiet. That's when he's angriest.

know: Gold Line was his mother's jewelry store. He kept her name on the license.
He's never raised his own hand to anybody. He considers that a point of honor.
His nephew is supposed to take over. Sal thinks the kid is soft, and he's privately glad.
sal.cold: Sal doesn't look up. "Buying or selling. I got nothing else for you."
sal.v: Polite, precise, old-fashioned. Never raises his voice. Everything is a transaction and he says so pleasantly. Dry opera-fan wit.

treat: Buy the gym a new heavy bag

mood.up: June's shadowboxing between rounds of yelling at people. Good day.
mood.flat: June's taping somebody's hands, not saying much.
mood.down: June's sitting on the ring apron, staring at an unpaid power bill.

know: She went 14 and 2 as a pro. The two were the same woman. She still has the tape.
She's kept the gym free for kids under sixteen since the day she bought it.
She trains Tasha, sixteen, like a daughter. First fight's coming and June can't sleep.
june.cold: June points at the door with a focus mitt. "Not in my gym."
june.v: Blunt, sparing with words, a coach to the bone. Says hard things plainly and kind things almost never. Respects people who show up.

treat: Bring coffee and a bear claw

mood.up: Tommy's got the radio on the oldies station and a rare smile.
mood.flat: Tommy's under a hood, grunting at a seized bolt.
mood.down: Tommy's sitting on an upturned bucket holding his lower back.

know: He's rebuilt every pump and supercharger on this lake since 1979. He can hear a bad wear ring from the parking lot.
His wife did the books until she passed. He hasn't opened the ledger since.
He doesn't have kids. He's been waiting for somebody worth handing the keys to.
tommy.cold: Tommy wipes his hands and keeps wiping. "We're full up. Try somewhere else."
tommy.v: Gruff, tired, grumbles in shop talk. Compliments come out sideways. Goes quiet about his wife. Loves the machines more than he will say.

mood.up: Kowalski's telling Rosa a joke at the counter. She's heard it.
mood.flat: Kowalski's doing the crossword in pen.
mood.down: Kowalski's stirring his coffee and not drinking it.

know: Twenty-two years on the same six blocks. He knows whose kid you are before you say it.
He's four years from a pension and has stopped pretending the job is what he signed up for.
He lets slip that his best source on the docks eats a lot of sunflower seeds.
kow.cold: Kowalski sets his cup down. "Sit somewhere else."
kow.v: Weary beat cop, deadpan. Has heard every story and says so. Dry, patient, not cruel. Counts the years to his pension.
